newsitem.title: UK: Small UK companies' orders grow modestly - CBI.
newsitem.headline: Small UK companies' orders grow modestly - CBI.

text.p: British small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) have enjoyed a moderate increase in orders, matching the performance of the rest of manufacturing industry, the Confederation of British Industry said on Monday.
A survey by the CBI and Pannell Kerr Forster found a positive balance of six percent of SMEs said orders rose over the four months to February and a further pick-up is expected.

"Our survey shows that small- and medium-sized enterprises are keeping pace with the rest of the manufacturing sector in terms of new orders and output and doing better on the jobs front," said Tony Bonner, chairman of the CBI's SME council.
Ten percent more SMEs reported an increase in output over the past four months than reported a fall.
In contrast, export orders fell at their fastest rate since October 1992. A negative balance of eight percent of SMEs reported lower export demand despite positive prior expectations.
Domestic prices for SMEs fell for the fourth quarterly survey in a row -- five percent more companies reported price falls than rises. For manufacturing industry as a whole, prices remain flat.
SMEs' export prices fell at their sharpest rate since October 1992 with a balance of 16 percent of firms reporting price falls.
"Competitive pressures in the home market combined with the continued strength of sterling have led to a sharp fall in both domestic and export prices for SMEs," Bonner said.

The smaller companies continued to outperform the rest of the industry on the employment front. On average, they experienced stable employment while manufacturing as a whole experienced a marked downturn, the survey found. A further pick-up in SME employment is expected over the next four months.
